entries.title: Practical unit conversion, including squared and cubed quantities
entries.whyHeld: SI-prefix half of the requirement had no in-batch citation after an unpermitted-class/unsupported source was removed in a prior audit.
entries.resolution: Formally recorded as a structured satisfaction: the already-VERIFIED, accepted Batch 01 mastery FM-LP-19 (engineering notation and SI unit prefixes) independently covers the SI-prefix mechanism, and EQCT-LP-02 already depends on it as a cross-domain prerequisite. The squared/cubed half remained separately and directly evidenced throughout (SRC-LIBRETEXTS-SQCUBIC).

entries.title: Power: meaning, quantity symbol, unit, and distinction from energy and power factor
entries.whyHeld: The DISTINCTION dimension's dimensionless-power-factor claim rested on a disclosed inference (P/S=W/VA cancellation), not retrieved text.
entries.resolution: A direct, explicit, permitted-class (AUTHORITATIVE_EDUCATIONAL_REFERENCE) passage was found and read: LibreTexts/Kuphaldt states plainly that power factor "is a unitless quantity".

entries.title: Power factor: meaning, notation, dimensionless nature, and distinction from power
entries.whyHeld: Narrowed from 3 unresolved dimensions to 1: DISTINCTION and QUANTITY_SYMBOL are now resolved (see below), but UNIT_SYMBOL (power factor's formal dimensionless/no-unit attestation) has no permitted-class (PRIMARY_NORMATIVE_OR_STANDARDS_BODY / PROFESSIONAL_BODY / AUTHORITATIVE_TECHNICAL_REFERENCE) source that explicitly states it -- IEC's own power-factor entry (IEV 131-11-46) is silent on unit, unlike sibling entries; only a general BIPM 'unit one' principle applies via disclosed inference, and LibreTexts' explicit statement is not a permitted class for this SYMBOL_OR_CONVENTION-mode dimension.
entries.resolution: DISTINCTION resolved via LibreTexts explicit statement (see EQCT-LP-05 route); QUANTITY_SYMBOL resolved via IEC Electropedia IEV 131-11-46 (symbol lambda, correcting the prior "cos phi"/"p.f." assumption). UNIT_SYMBOL remains genuinely unresolved after a real, bounded, permitted-class-respecting search (IEC Electropedia, BIPM SI Brochure, targeted web search for IEC/ISO/IEEE/NIST statements) -- not fabricated closed.

entries.resolution: IEC Electropedia IEV 103-06-02 (PRIMARY_NORMATIVE_OR_STANDARDS_BODY) independently confirms the symbol f.

entries.title: Capacitance: meaning, quantity symbol and unit

entries.resolution: IEC Electropedia IEV 131-12-13 (PRIMARY_NORMATIVE_OR_STANDARDS_BODY) independently confirms the symbol C.

entries.title: Inductance: meaning, quantity symbol and unit
entries.whyHeld: Sole QUANTITY_SYMBOL source reclassified to an unpermitted authority class.
entries.resolution: IEC Electropedia IEV 131-12-19 (PRIMARY_NORMATIVE_OR_STANDARDS_BODY) confirms symbol L; the related reactance/inductive-reactance entries (IEV 131-12-46/131-12-47) are disclosed alongside for the shared row with EQCT-LP-12.

entries.title: Inductive reactance: meaning, unit, and distinction from inductance
entries.whyHeld: DISTINCTION's prior source sentence was fabricated (not present on the cited page); QUANTITY_SYMBOL's sole source was reclassified to an unpermitted authority class.
entries.resolution: DISTINCTION restored via two genuinely-read, permitted-class (AUTHORITATIVE_EDUCATIONAL_REFERENCE) sources read together: inductance's own definition contains no frequency term (SRC-ETW-INDUCTOR), while reactance's own formula X=omega*L explicitly contains an angular-frequency multiplier (SRC-LIBRETEXTS-REACTANCE). QUANTITY_SYMBOL resolved the same way as EQCT-LP-11 (shared evidence row).

entries.title: Ohmmeter: measures resistance
entries.whyHeld: No verbatim passage had ever actually been captured for this specific requirement, despite the underlying fact not being in doubt.
entries.resolution: IEC Electropedia IEV 313-01-09 supplies a direct, exact sentence: "ohmmeter, resistance meter -- instrument intended to measure electrical resistance."

entries.title: Fleming's right-hand (generator) rule
entries.whyHeld: No permitted-class source was found and read in text form stating the exact thumb=motion/first-finger=field/second-finger=current mapping specifically for the RIGHT-hand GENERATOR rule (not the left-hand motor rule, not the unrelated grip rule).
entries.resolution: Two further dedicated re-sourcing attempts (one via a background research agent, one independently by the primary session) confirmed a genuine citation trail (Wikipedia -> Hughes, "Electrical & Electronic Technology", 12th ed., p.145) but could not render/read that textbook page through any available tool. Sources found and explicitly rejected as confusable-but-different rules (motor rule, grip rule) were correctly excluded rather than misused. Remains a genuine, bounded, honestly-disclosed gap.

entries.title: The simple AC generator: parts and how they work together
entries.whyHeld: Narrowed from 2 unresolved requirements (single-loop-alternator-generator-parts, coil) to 1 (coil only); slip-rings and brushes were already VERIFIED.
entries.resolution: single-loop-alternator-generator-parts is now VERIFIED: DOE Fundamentals Handbook Module ES-07 "Basic AC Theory" (a different module of the same already-accepted handbook family) explicitly and repeatedly describes a genuinely single loop ("a conductor, or loop of wire" / "a conductor loop"), fully labelled with field, slip rings and brushes. The coil's own standardised schematic-SYMBOL geometry remains genuinely unresolved: IEC 60617 is login-gated, and a real IEEE Std 315-1975/ANSI Y32.2-1975 lead (Section 6.2, naming inductor/coil/winding symbols) was found but its only located copy is truncated before the relevant page.

entries.title: Recognising the schematic symbols for Unit 202 components
entries.whyHeld: This is a breadth requirement over all 15 AC6.2 component families. 13 of 15 already have real, directly-read symbol geometry from IEEE Std 315-1975/ANSI Y32.2-1975 (PRIMARY_NORMATIVE_OR_STANDARDS_BODY, disclosed foreword-claimed IEC-117/predecessor compatibility). 2 of 15 (LED, inverter) have no dedicated named symbol in that 1975 standard -- only a general symbol plus an inserted letter code, which is genuinely how that standard represents them, not a sourcing failure. Separately, the CURRENT IEC 60617 database's own free preview confirms 6 relevant ID/name pairs (including LED as S01919) but not their artwork/geometry or Standard/Obsolete status, both of which sit behind a paid login not accessed in this pass.
entries.resolution: No further external acquisition was attempted this pass beyond confirming the existing record; the paid IEC 60617 login is a genuine, disclosed access barrier, and the 1975 standard's own lack of dedicated LED/inverter symbols is a fact about the standard, not an unresolved search. Remains an honestly bounded partial.
